summary: Bounded work package: made PyTorch/ROCm training work on the gfx1151 integrated GPU and measured it. Installed torch 2.13.0+rocm7.1 into .venv-rocm and AMD's gfx1151-specific torch 2.9.1+rocm7.13.0a into .venv-rocm-therock; diagnosed two defects in the pytorch.org wheel on this host (bundled ROCr segfaults on first HSA queue creation, fixed by LD_PRELOAD of the system ROCr; bundled MIOpen cannot assemble its BatchNorm training kernel on gfx1151, worked around with GroupNorm) and rejected the seemingly obvious MIOpen LD_PRELOAD fix after showing it loads a second HIP runtime and corrupts the heap. Wrote a correctness-and-throughput harness (bench.py), an environment helper (activate.sh) and a standalone bug reproducer, and produced the GPU enablement report. Incidentally found and characterised a multithreaded OpenBLAS SGEMM data race on this Zen 5 host that silently corrupts numpy float32 linear algebra.
validationPerformed: GPU numerical correctness scored against float64 references rather than CPU fp32: 4096x4096 fp32 matmul relative error 3.45e-06, bf16 matmul 3.03e-03, MLP gradients 1.65e-08, Drop7 residual-CNN forward 1.13e-06 and gradients 3.28e-07.
200-step GPU training soak at batch 1024 with GroupNorm: all parameters finite, loss fell from 2.95 to 0.003 on a fixed batch.
Native HIP vector-add compiled with system hipcc for gfx1151 returned exact results, isolating the segfault to the wheel's bundled ROCr rather than the driver or hardware.
OpenBLAS SGEMM race established as software, not silicon, by a same-process control arm: numpy/OpenBLAS 40/40 runs corrupt at 32 threads while torch/oneDNN was 0/40 on identical data.
Did NOT run make research-validate: this package created no theory, experiment, dataset, result or seed-lease record, and the repository tree was concurrently being written by other agents.
limitations: All throughput numbers were measured on a heavily contended host (mean 1-minute load 20-41 on 32 logical CPUs) because other agents held the machine for the whole session. They are reported as best-of-N, which bounds contention but does not eliminate it, and every table carries its observed load. They are lower bounds and should be re-measured on an idle host before any performance claim is promoted.
No gameplay was run, no seed was opened, and no policy or scientific conclusion is claimed.
BatchNorm training is unusable on the pytorch.org wheel on this target; the GroupNorm workaround is a model-architecture change that has not been evaluated for effect on learning quality.
The OpenBLAS finding is characterised but not reported upstream, and has not been tested against a distribution build, a from-source build, a newer OpenBLAS, or genuine SkylakeX hardware.
